notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Plates are long or short with a blue strip on the left, like Europe; taxi plates are deep red.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Arabic is official, but English and French are also common on signs.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: The only Middle Eastern country with official low-quality shitcam coverage.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Apart from the shitcam, coverage is Generation 3 trekker, mostly at tourist sites, campuses and trails.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Mediterranean look with many hills and rocky cliffs.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Metal mesh poles in several designs, sometimes painted bright yellow; plain wooden poles also occur.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Many buildings use sandstone blocks, like Jerusalem stone in Israel and the West Bank.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Most coverage is near the west coast, north of the capital.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Around Zahle are flat farm fields with mountains to the northwest; a visible black car appears here.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Snow on mountain tops or ground appears in the northeastern mountains.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The north is very flat and agricultural, with mountains to the southeast.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: The only covered city with many modern high-rises; the promenade has grey brick paving and many fan palms.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: An ancient coastal city of old buildings, nearly all unpainted stone blocks.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: A large complex of Roman ruins.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A large canyon lies to the south of the trekker near Bsharri.
